purpose: Every case the compatibility view asserts, and why. Each derived fixture is ONE named edit to bytes shipped by the pinned Engineering Assurance release, re-applied and compared by scripts/legacy_evidence_view.py on every run. A fixture that cannot be re-derived from the pinned source is a hand-written blob claiming to be one named change, and the view refuses it.
derivation_source: engineering_assurance/fixtures/verification-semantics/pgm01-v1.json and pgm01-v2.json, both digest-pinned in assurance/pins.json. The release's own known-good records are the only honest base for a derived fixture, because this repository retains no PGM-01 record of its own.
discrimination: Two cases return `unreadable` under the real record id and are separable only by the upstream reason text: an unknown check status (`unknown-check-status`) and a structurally undecodable body (`truncated-body`). map_pgm01_bytes offers no structural discriminator for that pair, so `expected_reason_contains` is used for them and the limitation is stated here rather than resolved by re-deriving a discriminator locally — which would mean writing the mapping this migration removed. Every other case asserts a structural field: `source_record_id`, `source_schema_version`, or `outcome`.

cases.why: The release's own v1 record, unedited. A mapping only ever observed refusing is indistinguishable from a step that never worked, so the census requires at least one positive control to be accepted before it can match.
The v2 positive control. It also supplies the `failed` state from a record the release itself ships, so `failed` is demonstrated by real bytes and not only by an edit this repository made.
One check's status becomes a failure. The mapping must carry a failure through as `failed` rather than folding it into the record's other passing check.
`error` is a distinct legacy state: a check that could not be run is not a check that ran and failed.
A check that ran and reached no verdict. It must not collapse into either a pass or a failure.
A check whose tool was absent. Distinct from skipped, which is a deliberate omission, and from error, which is a failed attempt.

A status the legacy vocabulary never defined. The mapping refuses the record rather than guessing which of the six states a novel word meant — which is the behaviour that keeps an unknown from silently becoming a pass. Note that `not-computed` is a perfectly good word in the NEW vocabulary; that it is unknown to the LEGACY one is exactly the point.
Bytes that are not a record at all. The mapping reports `unreadable-source` as the record id, because it cannot attribute an answer to a record whose identity it could not read.

A schema version the mapping does not cover. This is the same refusal this repository's own 12 retained envelopes receive, reproduced on a record whose other fields are known-good, so the refusal is shown to be about the version and not about the record being unusual.

Known-good bytes offered under an identity that is not theirs. The mapping refuses and says `tampered-source`, which is structurally distinct from `unreadable-source`, so tampering and undecodability are told apart by a field rather than by wording.

One of this repository's own retained envelopes, read as a declared case rather than only in the bulk census, so the refusal this migration reports is asserted by id and not merely observed in aggregate. agent-ix/engineering-assurance#21.
